newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: U.S. defends Soros, unaware of conspiracy on currency.
newsitem.headline: U.S. defends Soros, unaware of conspiracy on currency.

text.p: A U.S. State Department spokesman said over the weekend that Washington was not aware of any American-based conspiracy fuelling currency fluctuation problems in Southeast Asia and a spokesman defended financier George Soros.

"We're not aware of any conspiracy emanating from our country that would contribute to the current problems, the financial problems in this part of the world," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters Saturday.
Burns also defended international financier George Soros, an American who was blamed for destabilising Southeast Asian currencies for political motives by Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamed.
"George Soros is a highly respected individual in the United States who has done a lot of good things for many countries around the world, specifically in Central Europe," Burns said.

U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright briefly discussed the currency problems during talks on Saturday with Mahathir and Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Balawi but there was no discussion of the charges against Soros, Burns said.

The Association of Southeast Asian Nations Regional Forum over the weekend brought together the nine ASEAN countries, along with 11 countries from the West and Asia. ASEAN comprises Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore, Vietnam, the Philippines and Brunei and has formally accepted Laos and Burma as new members.

On Saturday, after a week of calling currency speculators "rogues," "robbers" and "brigands," Mahathir said: "Today I am confirming that George Soros was the man I was talking about." Mahathir also accused Soros of using his financial clout to try to block Burma's admission to ASEAN.
Mayalsia and neighbouring countries have seen attacks on their currencies in the past month forcing devaluations in Thailand and the Philippines and expensive intervention efforts in Malaysia.
